title: Log regularity of a marked nodal curve over a log regular pair
statement: Let $X,Y$ be Noetherian schemes, meaning quasi-compact locally Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $T\subseteq Y$ be a closed subset such that $(Y,T)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with all geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] nonempty connected one-dimensional schemes and smooth except at ordinary double points. An ordinary double point on a geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Assume $f$ is smooth over $Y\setminus T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor [def-weil-closed-immersion], locally cut out by one non-zero-divisor, contained in the smooth locus of $f$ and etale over $Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $B=|D|\cup f^{-1}(T)$ is nowhere dense and $(X,B)$ is a log regular pair.

source.place: Expose VI, Proposition 1.9 and its proof, printed pp. 70--71: log regularity of the marked nodal curve, with the local equation uv=h. The etale nodal local form also occurs in Stacks 0CBY, curves.tex, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-etale-chart]; finite presentation implies lfp by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The etale maps $W\to X$ and $V\to Y$ are lfp [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence lft: finite presentations give finite algebra generators [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $X,Y$ are locally Noetherian, so are $W,V$ [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Take affine $V$ around the base lift and restrict $W$ to its inverse image, retaining the source lift. Write $p:W\to X$, $g:W\to V$, $T_V=(V\to Y)^{-1}(T)$ (closed by continuity), $D_W=D\times_XW$ and $B_W=|D_W|\cup g^{-1}(T_V)=p^{-1}(B)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], $V\to Y$ is open: each nonempty open $H\subset V$ has nonempty open image meeting $Y\setminus T$, so $H$ meets $V\setminus T_V$. Both divisorial sheaves assign functions invertible off $T_V$ on etale test schemes over $V$. Pointed etale refinements identify ring/log stalks, units, structure maps, nonunit ideals, regular quotients, characteristic groups, dimensions and ranks. Fs charts restrict; triviality is $V\setminus T_V$. Thus [def-trf-log-regular-pair] gives $(V,T_V)$ log regular. The three forms have a base fs chart $P$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71; VI 1.4 and 1.8.

proof.text: For smooth and marked forms apply [lem-trf-smooth-marked-log-chart] over $(V,T_V)$, with $E=\varnothing$ or $E=D_W=V(z)$ and the supplied comparison. Its boundary is $B_W$. Its $P$ or $P\oplus\mathbf N$ structure is log regular and divisorial, with dense triviality locus $W\setminus B_W=p^{-1}(X\setminus B)$.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71; VI 1.4 and 1.8.

proof.text: For the nodal form write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$, $a\in P$, $\varepsilon\in A^\times$. Apply [lem-trf-nodal-log-chart-realization] to the supplied etale $c:W\to\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-h))$, with $h$ invertible off $T_V$. Its $Q$-chart retains both branch generators. Since $D_W=\varnothing$, its dense triviality locus is $g^{-1}(V\setminus T_V)=W\setminus B_W$; it is divisorial and log regular.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71; VI 1.4 and 1.8.

proof.text: Choose a geometric point in nonempty open $O\subset X$ and a chart lift $w\in W$. The nonempty open $p^{-1}(O)$ meets dense $W\setminus B_W$, with image in $O\setminus B$. The marking is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion]; continuity makes $f^{-1}(T)$ closed. Thus $B$ is closed nowhere dense. Put $M=\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_{X\setminus B}^{\times}$. On etale test schemes over each chart both divisorial sheaves assign functions invertible on the same complement. These inclusions agree on overlaps, giving $M$ fs charts and triviality exactly $X\setminus B$. For $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$, equip $W\times_XH$ with the induced geometric point for each pointed etale neighbourhood $H$ of $\bar x$. This refines $H$ to a neighbourhood over $W$; every pointed neighbourhood over $W$ is over $X$ by composition. These refinements compute the same ring/log stalks, units and structure maps, hence the same ideals $I$, regular quotients $A/I$ and characteristic groups. Both Krull dimensions and rank agree; the children's dimension equality gives [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, printed pp. 70--71; VI 1.4 and 1.8.

proof_origin.place: Expose VI 1.4, 1.8, Proposition 1.9 and its proof, printed pp. 69--71; etale local model cross-checked with Stacks 0CBY.
